1.
Counter affidavit filed today in Court is taken no record.
2. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA and perused the record.
Learned counsel for respondent no.2 is not present.

3. The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.36 of 2023, under Section 363, 366, 376 IPC &
Section 3/4 of POCSO Act, P.S. Mawai, District Ayodhya.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant draws my attention to the FIR which was registered as a missing person report.
Subsequently, in the statement under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., the victim stated that they were known to each other for the last one year and were in love.

It was also stated that she had asked the applicant to take her failing which she would commit suicide and thereafter,
she went to Delhi and in fact, married.
5. Learned AGA opposes the bail application by arguing that as per the transfer certificate on record at Page 22 of the counter affidavit, the age of the victim is around 16 years and 2 months.
6. Learned counsel for the applicant argues that the transfer certificate is not a document prescribed under the Juvenile Justice Act and the rules framed thereunder.

7. Considering the submissions raised at the Bar, the statement under Section 161 & 164 Cr.P.C.,
clearly do not support the prosecution story; the final determination with regard to age shall be done at the time of trial in view of the law as explained in the case of Monish vs. State of U.P. & Ors.

sentences.text: As such, the applicant who is in custody since 09.05.2023 coupled with the fact that in the sole case of criminal antecedent against the applicant, he has been discharged which is duly disclosed in Para 17, the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
In view thereof, the application is allowed.

8. Let the applicant Dileep Kumar be released on bail in aforesaid FIR number on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
